newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CAPE FARMERS IN S.AFRICA PLEASED WITH RAIN, COLD.
newsitem.headline: CAPE FARMERS IN S.AFRICA PLEASED WITH RAIN, COLD.

text.p: Wheat, grape and deciduous fruit producers in South Africa's Western Cape province are pleased with the season's cold, wet conditions so far, farming spokesman Frik Bosman said on Tuesday.
"Our wheat farmers are overjoyed," Bosman told Reuters, referring to heavy rains in recent weeks over the region which grows about half the country's winter wheat crop.
The total national crop, harvested in November, came in at around 2.7 million tonnes for 96/97.
Bosman, director of the Western Cape Agricultural Union, said most of the wheat planted this year was just beginning to germinate and it was too early to predict tonnages.
"But if things continue like now, we should have an excellent year," he said.

Bosman said cold weather over the last few days, which has brought snow to Western Cape mountains, was good news for grape growers and deciduous fruit farmers. Cold weather in winter enhances fruit development.
He said the region had experienced some localised flooding which had harmed some vegetable and citrus crops.
